**Issue #2901 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2901: CI: super run failed on a production candidate
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 41585437366](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41585437366) on #2892, the promotion of `87e53f887bb2` into production, failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [e2e (7/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41585437366/job/125753199866) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: production waits on this run, so it is yours and it comes first (`priority:high`). #2892 promotes `87e53f887bb2`, a commit of `main`, so the fix lands on `main` like any other. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). Say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them. Once the fix is on `main`, a person comments `/promote` on the production issue, which tests the newer commit.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41591845288)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Get super run job **e2e (7/8)** green on `main`. I reproduced it on this branch's base (`df034cc15`, whose `apps/` and `e2e/` match the failing `87e53f887`) by running shard 7 with the job's own commands. 74 tests passed and 1 failed: spec 38, `/ (phone)`, on both attempts. axe reports `label-content-name-mismatch` (serious, WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name) on `.landing-news-bookmark`.

The root cause is a real accessibility bug from #2885. The News bookmark's name is `aria-label="News"`, but the only text it shows is the unclaimed count. That count is an `aria-hidden` span, and axe's rule counts `aria-hidden` text as visible. Spec 38's desktop `/` passes only because it runs before any sign-in. The phone `/` runs signed in as p1, because `signedIn` in `e2e/support/commands.ts` lasts for the whole spec file, so the bookmark is drawn there.

Done means:
- each landing bookmark's accessible name includes the count it shows;
- unit tests hold that rule on every pull request;
- spec 38 passes at both widths, checked locally (the pull request's CI does not run spec 38);
- the pull request says it makes `e2e (7/8)` pass, and how that was checked.

## Files to touch

| File | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/routes/landing.tsx` | change | `QuestsBookmark` and `NewsBookmark`: the button's `aria-label` includes the count when the bubble shows |
| `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` | change | two entries: `"Quests, {count} held"` and `"News, {count} to claim"` |
| `apps/web/src/routes/landing-news.test.tsx` | change | accessible-name assertions in three existing `R2875002` tests |
| `apps/web/src/routes/landing-quests.test.tsx` | change | accessible-name assertions in two existing `R2035000` tests |

Do not touch:
- `e2e/` (spec 38, `support/a11y.ts`, `support/axe-exceptions.ts`, `support/commands.ts`);
- `spec/`, any crate, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`.

The rulings that govern the bookmarks are R2875002 (News) and R2035000 (Quests); the spec section is §14.13. Neither says what a bookmark's accessible name is. This is presentation, not a rules decision, so it needs no new ruling, no `spec/pending` paragraph and no patch fragment (no card plays differently).

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/routes/landing.tsx`, `function QuestsBookmark`.**
   - Right after `const held = quests?.quests.length ?? 0;` (about line 424), add:
     ```tsx
     // WCAG 2.5.3 (spec 38's axe check): the name holds the count the bubble shows.
     const questsName = held > 0 ? t("Quests, {count} held", { count: formatNumber(held) }) : t("Quests");
     ```
   - In the `<button className="landing-quests-bookmark" …>`, change `aria-label={t("Quests")}` to `aria-label={questsName}`.
   - Leave `title={t("Quests")}`, the `aria-hidden="true"` on the count span, and everything else as they are.

2. **`apps/web/src/routes/landing.tsx`, `function NewsBookmark`.**
   - Right after `const unclaimed = news.filter((entry) => !entry.claimed).length;` (about line 480), add:
     ```tsx
     // WCAG 2.5.3 (spec 38's axe check): the name holds the count the bubble shows.
     const newsName = unclaimed > 0 ? t("News, {count} to claim", { count: formatNumber(unclaimed) }) : t("News");
     ```
   - Change `aria-label={t("News")}` to `aria-label={newsName}`. Leave `title={t("News")}` as it is.
   - `formatNumber` and `t` are already imported (line 19).
   - Use a comma, never parentheses. axe's `curateTokens` strips parentheticals, so a name like "News (2)" still fails.

3. **`apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`.** Add each entry right after the existing key it extends. The `{count}` token must appear in both the key and its value, or the i18n test fails.
   - After `"Quests": "任务",` add `"Quests, {count} held": "任务，持有 {count} 个",`
   - After `"News": "新闻",` add `"News, {count} to claim": "新闻，{count} 条待领取",`

4. **`apps/web/src/routes/landing-news.test.tsx`.**
   - In `it("R2875002 the bookmark sits beside the quests' with a red count of the unclaimed entries")`, line 113: change `toHaveAccessibleName("News")` to `toHaveAccessibleName("News, 2 to claim")`. Put this comment above it: `// WCAG 2.5.3 (spec 38): the name holds the count the bubble shows.`
   - In `it("R2875002 all claimed shows no count")`, after `expect(screen.queryByTestId(landingTestid.newsCount)).toBeNull();`, add `expect(bookmark).toHaveAccessibleName("News");`
   - In `it("R2875002 a claim takes the count down by one once the server answers")`, right after the `waitFor` that sees the count at `"1"`, add `expect(screen.getByTestId(landingTestid.newsBookmark)).toHaveAccessibleName("News, 1 to claim");`

5. **`apps/web/src/routes/landing-quests.test.tsx`.**
   - In `it("R2035000 the bookmark hangs on the doors' box with the held count, closed")`, line 88: change `toHaveAccessibleName("Quests")` to `toHaveAccessibleName("Quests, 2 held")`, with the same comment as in step 4.
   - In `it("R2035000 none held but one due says No quests yet., counts down, and shows no count")`, after `expect(screen.queryByTestId(landingTestid.questsCount)).toBeNull();`, add `expect(bookmark).toHaveAccessibleName("Quests");`

6. **Run the unit tests and the checks** listed under Tests.

7. **Run spec 38 against a built client**, as the super run does. This is the proof for the pull request. All commands run from the repository root; `$T` is `${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}`.
   1. `cargo build --release -p jackioh-server -p jackioh-tools`
   2. `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm --dir apps/web exec vite build --mode development` (this is `pnpm build:e2e`).
   3. Start the server in the background: `E2E=1 CATALOG_VERSION=$("$T"/release/jackioh catalog-version) "$T"/release/jackioh-server > /tmp/server.log 2>&1`. Wait for `server.listening` in the log.
   4. Start the client in the background: `E2E=1 pnpm --dir apps/web exec vite preview --port 5173 --strictPort`
   5. Run the spec: `cd e2e && E2E=1 pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec cypress/e2e/38-accessibility.cy.ts`. Expect 51 passing. `/ (phone)` should log `[axe] / (phone): 1 serious or critical, 0 not excepted`; the one left is the `.landing-fan-card` exception.
   6. Optionally run the whole shard: `cd e2e && E2E=1 pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec "$(node scripts/shard-specs.mjs 7 8)"`. Specs 13, 25, 31 and 48 fold their logs through `target/release/jackioh` under the repository root (`e2e/support/tasks/replay-runner.ts`). When `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` points elsewhere, link it in as `target` first, and `unlink target` afterwards so it is not committed.
   7. Stop both background processes.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/routes/landing-news.test.tsx`: the three assertions from step 4. Together they check that the name is "News, 2 to claim" with two unclaimed, "News, 1 to claim" after a claim, and "News" with none.
- `apps/web/src/routes/landing-quests.test.tsx`: the two assertions from step 5. They check "Quests, 2 held" with two held, and "Quests" with none held.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/i18n.test.ts`, unchanged. Its tests `R711000 every sentence the client wraps in t() has a zh-CN entry` and `R711000 every zh-CN.json dictionary entry has matching parameter tokens with its English key` cover step 3.
- Before step 1, the first assertion in each of steps 4 and 5 fails against the current code: the name is "News" or "Quests" alone.

Commands:
```
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/routes/landing-news.test.tsx src/routes/landing-quests.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/routes/landing.tsx apps/web/src/routes/landing-news.test.tsx apps/web/src/routes/landing-quests.test.tsx
```
Then run spec 38 as in step 7.

## Done when

- [ ] Both bookmarks' `aria-label` include the count whenever the bubble shows (steps 1–2), and both zh-CN entries exist (step 3).
- [ ] The vitest files above pass; typecheck and eslint are clean.
- [ ] Spec 38 passes locally with 51 of 51 (step 7). The pull request description says:
  - it fixes super run 41585437366's `e2e (7/8)` (spec 38, `/ (phone)`, `label-content-name-mismatch` on `.landing-news-bookmark`);
  - the cause is #2885's News bookmark;
  - how it was checked: the commands of step 7 and the before and after results.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests.
- [ ] No tracked file outside the four above changed. No `target` symlink, `e2e/artifacts/` or `apps/web/dist/` is committed (the last two are gitignored).

## Risks

- **Hidden information and rule 7:** none. The name uses only the count the client already shows, which comes from the server's answer.
- **The i18n guard:** the English keys must be the literal first argument of `t()`, and both zh-CN values must hold `{count}`. Otherwise `i18n.test.ts` fails.
- **A different name in another test:** no other test or spec reads these bookmarks by name. I searched `apps/web/src` and `e2e` for `name: "Quests"`, `name: "News"`, `questsBookmark` and `newsBookmark`.
- **A stale axe exception:** spec 38 fails on an exception that no longer fires. None is added or removed here, and the `/` and `/ (phone)` `.landing-fan-card` exceptions still fire, as the run shows.
- **Proof:** the pull request's CI does not run spec 38 (it is not in `SMOKE`), so step 7's local run is the only proof before the next super run. Report what was actually seen.

## Decisions taken (the task did not settle them)

- **Fix the name rather than spec 38.**
  - Rejected: making the phone pass's public pages sign out. That hides a defect every active account meets.
  - Rejected: adding an axe exception. Exceptions record design decisions (`axe-exceptions.ts`), and this one has a plain fix.
- **Fix the Quests bookmark too.** It has the same markup. It would fail spec 38 the day p1 holds a quest under E2E, while today it shows no count.
  - Rejected: leaving it for another issue.
- **Name wording.** "News, {count} to claim" follows R2875002's "unread is unclaimed"; "Quests, {count} held" follows R2035000's "held count".
  - Rejected: parentheses, because axe drops parentheticals.

## Open questions

- In `e2e/support/commands.ts`, `signedIn` lasts for the rest of a spec file. So spec 38's phone "public pages" and "practice and hotseat, no account" tests have run signed in as p1 since #1561. A person may want those tests signed out, with a deliberate signed-in `/` check added at both widths. That changes what spec 38 covers, so it is left out here.
- Planner's evidence, from this machine with Chrome 156: shard 7 at `df034cc15` gave 74 passing and 1 failing (spec 38, `/ (phone)`, both attempts). I could not read the CI log itself. It is the same failure unless that job also failed somewhere else; specs 10, 13, 15, 17, 25, 31 and 48 all passed locally.
````
